home.seoDescription: Explore Jalaranu's underlake datacenter project, validation approach, and partnership opportunities for computing infrastructure in Indonesia.

hero.h1: Computing infrastructure **beneath the lake**. Supporting Indonesia's ==digital resilience==.
intro: Jalaranu is developing a modular underlake datacenter project. The focus is to evaluate **thermal efficiency, operational reliability**, and the feasibility of deployment in Indonesia.
We welcome collaboration with investors, institutions, and technology partners to establish a measurable foundation for development.

why.h2: Why consider a location **beneath a lake**?
body: Underwater placement offers a different approach to heat management, physical space, and infrastructure access. Its potential benefits need to be assessed alongside the implications for deployment, maintenance, connectivity, and recovery.
The central question is: under what conditions would this approach be more feasible than a land-based datacenter using water-based cooling?
Jalaranu places that comparison at the centre of its evaluation.

technology.seoDescription: Explore the Jalaranu project: from shore facilities and computing modules to heat management, connectivity, and recovery.

hero.h1: Engineering starts with the right questions.
hero.body: Jalaranu explores the underlake datacenter as **one complete system**. Module placement needs to be evaluated together with power, networking, heat management, maintenance, and recovery.

architecture.h2: From shore interfaces to the underwater environment.
body: The project architecture includes four elements: shore-based support facilities, power and communications connections, the computing module, and monitoring and operational management. Their relationships determine how the overall facility can function and recover.
Early visualisations use a truncated square pyramid. This is a design exploration; final geometry, materials, and specifications will follow engineering and test findings.
architecture.visualNote: A block diagram and cross-section showing logical connections, without coordinates or facility-security details.
architecture.imageAlt: Engineering figure of the truncated-pyramid module: front elevation, section A-A, roof framing plan, and watertight joint detail.
architecture.imageCaption: Dimensional engineering draft, not a fabrication drawing.

items.title: Heat management
items.body: **Water conditions, heat transfer**, computing loads, and the energy required by supporting systems.

items.title: Module integrity
items.body: **The ability of structures, joints, and system interfaces** to withstand the defined operating conditions.

items.title: Power and connectivity
items.body: **Service needs, redundancy options**, behaviour during connection failures, and recovery procedures.

items.title: Maintenance
items.body: **What can be monitored remotely**, when intervention is required, and how the module can be handled or retrieved.

items.title: Security and control
items.body: **Administrative access, event monitoring, key management**, operator responsibilities, and protection of physical and digital interfaces.

comparison.h2: Advantages need to be assessed against relevant alternatives.
body: Evaluation should compare the underlake project with land-based solutions using equivalent service requirements, workloads, and assumptions. Relevant comparisons include land-based facilities with conventional cooling and water-based cooling, where applicable to the site under study.

Assessment covers energy, capital expenditure, operating costs, maintenance, connectivity, recovery, environmental effects, and end of life. Potential savings in one component do not in themselves demonstrate a lower total cost.

intro: The underlake project is evaluated against three reference placements at equal service: a terrestrial facility, a hardened bunker, and an undersea deployment. Each trade-off below is an initial assessment to be tested, not a measured result.

A companion ten-year cost model at equal service gives 6.00 million dollars for a terrestrial facility with conventional cooling, 6.34 for a hardened terrestrial facility with lake-water cooling, and 7.85 for the submerged design. Submersion buys capability, not cost saving.
placements.note: Initial framework assessment for discussion. Figures and rankings require measurement and site studies. Screening thermal numbers (a basin-average anomaly of about 0.001 kelvin over fifty years and a twelve-month footprint of 228-509 metres) carry unproven status until measured.

items.title: Terrestrial datacenter
items.body: The mature reference point: established supply chains, easy access, and proven operations. Its costs include energy-intensive cooling, land requirements, and the concentration of strategic data in a few urban corridors. At equal service the ten-year model gives 6.00 million dollars with conventional cooling; the strategic weakness is concentration in a few urban corridors.

items.title: Hardened bunker
items.body: Strong physical protection for critical workloads. The trade-offs are high construction cost, more complex heat rejection, and a facility that is harder to scale than modular surface infrastructure. At 6.34 million dollars with lake-water cooling it is the cheapest hardened comparator in the model, but it carries high construction cost and complex heat rejection.

items.title: Undersea datacenter
items.body: Proven at sea by Project Natick: ocean water removes heat without mechanical cooling. But the maritime threat surface includes submarine cable interception, anchor drag, and contested jurisdiction, with saltwater corrosion and difficult access. Project Natick proved submerged heat rejection at sea; the paper's threat model nonetheless treats the maritime surface (submarine cable interception, anchor drag, contested jurisdiction) as the decisive difference.

items.title: Underlake datacenter
items.body: A lake is not a small ocean. Inland waters sit inside domestic jurisdiction, beyond submarine reach, in quiet freshwater near hydropower and existing communities. Open questions remain: thermal and ecological effects, seismic exposure, acoustic hardening, and retrieval procedures. The model prices the submerged design at 7.85 million dollars: submersion removes direct maritime access paths and keeps the facility in domestic jurisdiction, but thermal, ecological, seismic, acoustic, and retrieval questions remain open and unproven.

body: The project can be evaluated for dedicated computing, storage, or particular infrastructure requirements defined by an organisation. The suitability of each use case must be established through requirements assessment and test evidence.
A use case mentioned here is not a statement that the service is already available or approved to handle sensitive data.

intro: The reference structure breaks the module into 24 numbered components across six systems. The figure is a dimensional engineering draft, not a fabrication drawing.

items.title: Protective enclosure
items.body: Stainless-steel shell, structural stiffeners, and corrosion protection, carried by a ballast skid. Lifting loads pass through four upper padeyes, while the service lid keeps two seals separated by a monitored interspace.

items.title: Computing cassette
items.body: An 8U cassette holds three 2U servers with SSD/NVMe storage and a network switch, under a proposed nitrogen atmosphere with controlled humidity and A/B power and fibre feedthroughs.

items.title: Cooling loop
items.body: A gas-to-liquid coil and fans move heat into a closed coolant circuit through A/B pumps and A/B external heat exchangers. Isolation valves separate branches, and lake water never mixes with internal coolant.

items.title: Power resilience
items.body: An optional LiFePO4 battery UPS sits in a lower bay separated from the computing equipment, targeting a ten-minute reserve at the assumed 2.1 kW load.

items.title: Vibration isolation
items.body: Four captive isolators with cushioned snubbers suspend the server cassette, with flexible connections, electrical bonding, and transport and service locks.

items.title: Monitoring and safety
items.body: Temperature, humidity, oxygen, pressure, and motion sensors, a camera with window and wiper, and a leak-detection tray feed power distribution and safety controls.

inside.note: All stated values are design assumptions, not measurements. Watertightness, operating depth, lifting capacity, and seismic resistance remain to be established through analysis and integrated testing.

validation.seoTitle: Technical, Economic and Environmental Validation | Jalaranu
validation.seoDescription: Learn about Jalaranu's test questions and staged approach to evaluating the feasibility of an underlake datacenter.

hero.h1: Evidence provides the basis for the next step.
hero.body: The feasibility of an underlake datacenter needs to be assessed **technically, economically, and environmentally**. Jalaranu's validation approach focuses on testable questions, explainable methods, and findings presented alongside their limitations.

items: The development stage will be announced once it has been confirmed.
The current focus, the latest update, and any evidence approved for sharing will be published as they become available.

plan.h2: Questions that shape the test programme.
plan.body: Success criteria, methods, and responsibilities need to be defined before testing begins.

table.question: How does the system perform across defined workloads and environmental conditions?
Do the module and its interfaces meet the specified operating and test conditions?
How does the system respond to disruptions, recover, and undergo maintenance?
How do installation, operation, intervention, retrieval, and end-of-life costs compare with alternatives?
How is the baseline documented, change monitored, and the evidence evaluated?
For which requirements and service levels do test results indicate suitability?

framework.h2: Staged development, with decisions at each stage.

steps.title: Requirements definition
steps.body: Establish objectives, relevant alternatives, and success criteria.

steps.title: Studies and preliminary engineering
steps.body: Assess candidate sites for further study, risks, system design, and cost assumptions.

steps.title: Component and integration testing
steps.body: Test the functions that determine system safety and performance.

steps.title: A limited pilot
steps.body: Measure performance within an agreed scope, supported by monitoring and recovery plans.

steps.title: Evaluation for the next stage
steps.body: Review findings, limitations, and the feasibility of further development.

framework.note: This sequence is a development framework, not a list of stages claimed to be complete.

body: Site studies need to consider water conditions, uses of the area, the needs of affected communities, and applicable requirements. The evaluation plan should cover baseline conditions, changes to monitor during testing, and the handling of facilities at end of life.
Study findings inform site and design decisions, including a decision not to proceed with an option if it is unsuitable.

items.title: Ecological discipline
items.body: The lake is the limiting resource; environmental benefit is never claimed without measurement.

items.title: A published thermal budget
items.body: Screening calculations give a basin-average anomaly of about 0.001 kelvin over fifty years and a twelve-month heat-equivalent footprint of 228-509 metres. Both stay unproven until measured at a candidate site.

items.title: Baseline before deployment
items.body: Baseline conditions, water conditions, area uses, and the needs of affected communities are part of the evaluation plan.

items.title: End of life
items.body: Decommissioning, retrieval, and lake restoration are planned from the start.

items.title: No-proceed stays valid
items.body: Where evidence is insufficient, an option is set aside rather than asserted.

results.body: Published findings and documents will appear here once they are available and approved for public release.

faq.a: **This website introduces the Jalaranu project and development opportunities.** Commercial service availability will be communicated separately once facility and service readiness have been confirmed.

**A lake is the deployment context being explored.** Suitability needs to be assessed against water conditions, access, energy, networking, environmental factors, and intended use. Selecting a lake does not in itself demonstrate an advantage over another location or design.

faq.q: Is the cooling free or energy-free?
faq.a: **The potential use of the water environment must be assessed alongside heat-transfer systems and the energy requirements of the whole facility.** Jalaranu does not claim specific savings without measured results and a clearly defined comparison.

faq.q: What happens if the module needs repair?
faq.a: **Monitoring, incident handling, retrieval, and component replacement are part of design evaluation.** Detailed procedures will follow the tested design and agreed service requirements.

faq.q: Can it support sensitive data or defence requirements?
faq.a: **Suitability needs to be assessed against data classification, system architecture, access controls, governance, and the requirements of the relevant institution.** This website does not claim approval or readiness to handle information at a particular classification level.

faq.q: How are effects on the lake assessed?
faq.a: **The study approach covers baseline conditions, changes to monitor, and evaluation during testing and at end of life.** Its scope must be adapted to the location and planned activities.

faq.q: How can I obtain more information?
faq.a: **Use the partnership form to introduce your organisation and the purpose of the discussion.** Information that can be shared will depend on the needs of the discussion and document availability.

partnerships.seoDescription: Explore collaboration with Jalaranu as an investor, government or defence institution, industry partner, or research organisation.

hero.h1: Start with the requirement. Agree on what needs to be demonstrated.
hero.body: Jalaranu welcomes conversations with organisations interested in evaluating, developing, or supporting the underlake datacenter project. Collaboration begins with **clear goals, realistic scope, and measurable results**.

body: We invite discussion of market needs, the business model, funding stages, and the evidence required at each stage. The initial focus is to understand how capital can reduce development uncertainty.
Topics include prospective users, available alternatives, cost estimates and their assumptions, capital requirements, and milestones for subsequent investment decisions.

tracks.h2: Evaluate strategic requirements through focused collaboration.
body: Discussion can begin with infrastructure needs, service continuity, operational control, data governance, and institutional evaluation criteria. The suitability of the Jalaranu project is determined through requirements assessment and relevant testing.

Potential collaboration may include feasibility studies, requirements definition, and the development of a limited pilot. Access requirements, information handling, and each party's responsibilities are agreed according to the scope of collaboration.

tracks.h2: Connecting engineering, infrastructure, and operational capabilities.
body: We welcome discussions with prospective partners in energy, connectivity, structures and manufacturing, computing, heat management, sensors, and field operations.
Contributions can be defined around development requirements, interface boundaries, integration responsibilities, and the test outcomes the parties aim to achieve together.

tracks.h2: Developing methods and evidence that can be reviewed.
body: Universities and research organisations can explore thermal, structural, reliability, economic, and environmental studies. Research scope, data use, publication, and rights to outcomes need to be agreed from the outset.

process.h2: From an initial conversation to a shared scope of work.
steps: Describe your organisation's requirements and objectives.
Discuss fit and the initial information that can be shared.
Define scope, contributions, and evaluation criteria.
Determine the next step based on both parties' readiness.

about.seoDescription: Discover Jalaranu's identity, development principles, and the people responsible for its underlake datacenter project.

hero.h1: Rooted in Indonesian identity. Developed through evidence.
hero.body: Jalaranu is an initiative developing an underlake datacenter project. We aim to bring **engineering, infrastructure requirements, and an understanding of the environment** into a measurable development process.

body: The name Jalaranu combines “jala”, understood as water in the naming of this brand, and “ranu”, lake. Its visual identity draws inspiration from Javanese heritage.
A guardian goddess supports a datacenter beneath flowing water. The symbol expresses a responsibility to safeguard knowledge and the infrastructure that supports it.
That meaning carries into the way the project is developed: clear questions, focused testing, and honest communication about findings and limitations.

sections.title: Scope of this notice
body: This page explains how contact information would be handled once the Jalaranu contact form and related processes are active. The current website is static and does not collect personal data by itself.

sections.title: Information we plan to collect
body: When the partnership form becomes active, the information requested will be limited to what is needed to review an enquiry: full name, organisation name, contact email, type of collaboration, and a message describing the organisation's needs.

sections.title: How the information would be used
body: The information would be used solely to review and respond to partnership enquiries, and to prepare follow-up discussions. It would not be used for marketing without consent and would not be sold to third parties.

sections.title: Storage, retention and access
body: Storage location, retention period, access controls, and the responsible data controller will be published here once the form and its processing practices are established. Until then, no form data is processed.

sections.title: Your rights and contact
body: Once processing begins, you will be able to request information about your data, corrections, or deletion through the contact channel published on this page. Use the partnership page contact form to reach the team about this notice.
